records.change: "as gods" becomes "as God"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew elohim can mean "God" or "gods". The serpent's promise is read as being like the one God rather than like divine beings.

records.change: "her Seed" and "He"/"His" capitalised; "it" becomes "He"
records.note: A translation choice: the Masoretic pronoun (hu) can be read "he" or "it", and the MKJV's capitals read the verse as a direct prophecy of Christ. The KJV leaves that reading to interpretation.

records.change: "digged down a wall" becomes "hamstrung a bull"
records.note: The Masoretic vowels read shor (ox) with a verb meaning to hamstring; the KJV reads shur (wall) and "dig down". The act of violence recalled is different, though no doctrine turns on it.

records.change: "none shut up, or left" becomes "only the imprisoned and abandoned remain"
records.note: A translation choice on the Hebrew ephes, which can mean "none" or "only"; the two readings say opposite things about who is left.

records.change: Capitalises "Commander" and "my Lord", treating the captain as divine
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew adoni ("my lord") is lower-case in the KJV; the MKJV's capitals identify the captain of the LORD's host as God himself. Both keep that Joshua worshipped him.

records.change: "fifty thousand and threescore and ten" becomes seventy, "including fifty chief men"
records.note: The Masoretic text has 50,070, which the KJV follows; some Hebrew manuscripts and Josephus have 70, and the MKJV reinterprets the "fifty". The number struck is very different.

records.change: "slew the brother of Goliath" becomes "killed one of Goliath"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads simply "Goliath"; the KJV supplies "the brother of" from 1 Chronicles 20:5, and the MKJV's "one of" is vaguer. Who Elhanan killed is left unclear.

records.change: Milcom called "the goddess" instead of "the god"
records.note: The Masoretic text uses the same word (elohei, "god of") for Chemosh and Milcom; the MKJV's "goddess" for Milcom has no basis in the Hebrew and looks like an error.

records.change: Omits "his son" after Rehoboam
records.note: "His son" (beno) is in the Masoretic text; the MKJV drops it. The parallel in 2 Chronicles 9:31 keeps "his son".

records.change: Omits "chosen": "chosen men, which were warriors" becomes "warriors"
records.note: The Masoretic text has bachur ("chosen"); the MKJV drops it. Small loss of detail, no doctrine affected.

records.change: "Thy son Benhadad" becomes "Your servant Ben-hadad"
records.note: The Masoretic text has binkha ("your son"), a courtesy title; the MKJV's "servant" is a paraphrase that changes the word.

records.change: Omits "his father" after Huram
records.note: The Masoretic text has Huram abiv ("Huram his father", probably a title of honour); the MKJV drops it. The same title appears in 2 Chronicles 2:13.

records.change: "How God was intreated of him" becomes "his entreaty"
records.note: The Hebrew (vehe'ater lo) says he was heard; the MKJV keeps only that he prayed. That God answered him is still stated in 2 Chronicles 33:13.

records.change: Omits "of heaven" from "the LORD God of heaven"
records.note: "God of heaven" (Elohei hashamayim) is in the Masoretic text; the MKJV drops it. The parallel Ezra 1:2 keeps the title.

records.change: "God shall cast upon him" becomes "it will hurl at him"
records.note: The Hebrew verb has no stated subject; the KJV supplies God, the MKJV takes it as the east wind of verse 21. The actor in the judgment changes.

records.change: "lower than the angels" becomes "lack a little from God"
records.note: The Hebrew is elohim; the KJV follows the Septuagint's "angels", which Hebrews 2:7 quotes of Christ, while the MKJV renders the Hebrew literally.

records.change: God remembers "the seekers of bloodshed", not the humble when avenging blood
records.note: A translation choice on doresh damim ("he who requires blood"); the KJV has God as the avenger who remembers the afflicted, the MKJV makes "them" the bloodthirsty.

records.change: "where their voice is not heard" becomes "their voice is not heard"
records.note: A translation choice with the same Hebrew: the KJV says the heavens' voice is heard in every language, the MKJV that their speech is silent. The universal witness is still stated in verse 4.

records.change: Command "worship him, all ye gods" becomes statement "all gods bow down"
records.note: The Hebrew hishtachavu can be imperative or past; the KJV's command matches Hebrews 1:6's use of the verse (from the Septuagint), which the MKJV's statement loses.

records.change: "Hell" becomes "Sheol"
records.note: The Hebrew is sheol; the KJV renders it "hell" here, the MKJV transliterates it, leaving open whether the place of the dead or of punishment is meant.

records.change: "must shew himself friendly" becomes "may be broken up"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew verb is taken as "come to ruin" rather than "be friendly". The first line becomes a warning about many friends instead of a duty of friendliness.

records.change: God rewarding fools becomes a saying about hiring a fool
records.note: The Hebrew is obscure and read many ways; the KJV makes it a statement about God's judgment, the MKJV a proverb about employers.

records.change: "Become his son" becomes "be his successor"
records.note: A translation choice on the rare Hebrew word manon, whose meaning is uncertain; the outcome for the pampered servant differs.

records.change: "set the world in their heart" becomes "set eternity"
records.note: The Hebrew olam can mean "world" or "eternity"; a translation choice that changes what God is said to have put in the human heart.

records.change: "O Lucifer" becomes "O shining star"
records.note: The Hebrew helel means "shining one"; "Lucifer" is the Vulgate's Latin for it. The MKJV's rendering loses the name long read as Satan's, though the verse is the same.

records.change: Sluices and fish ponds become broken foundations and wage-earners grieving
records.note: A translation choice for obscure Hebrew words; the MKJV reads different senses of the same consonants. The prophecy against Egypt stands either way.

records.change: Capitalises "sent Me", making the speaker divine
records.note: A translation choice on the same Hebrew: the MKJV's capitals read the speaker as God, sent by the Lord and his Spirit, a reading often taken as trinitarian; the KJV's lower-case "me" leaves it open.

records.change: Loses "others": gathering beyond Israel's outcasts becomes gathering "his gathered ones"
records.note: The Hebrew (od akabbets alav lenikbatsav) reads "yet I will gather to him, besides his gathered ones"; the MKJV's wording drops the promise of others, often read as the Gentiles, joining Israel.

records.change: "lift up a standard against him" becomes "make him flee"
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew verb nosesah (raise a banner, or put to flight). The Spirit's defeat of the enemy is kept, but the familiar image is lost.

records.change: "that troop" and "that number" become "Fortune" and "Fate"
records.note: The Hebrew Gad and Meni are taken as names of pagan deities rather than common nouns; a translation choice that makes the idolatry explicit.

records.change: "the heart of God" becomes "the heart of gods"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew elohim can be read as God or gods. The prince's claim to be divine is still stated ("I am a god").

records.change: "the heart of God" becomes "the heart of gods"
records.note: Translation choice over the Hebrew elohim, as in verse 2; the rebuke of the prince's pride is unchanged.

records.change: "I am God" becomes "I am of the gods"
records.note: Translation choice over the Hebrew elohim; the MKJV still has "not God" in the second half of the verse.

records.change: "my terror" becomes "his terror"
records.note: The written Hebrew text (ketiv) has "his terror" and the marginal reading (qere) "my terror"; the KJV follows the qere, the MKJV the ketiv.

records.change: "wind" and "breath" become "Spirit"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew ruach means wind, breath or spirit. The MKJV makes the life-giving breath God's Spirit, which verse 14 states anyway ("my spirit in you").

records.change: "chief prince" becomes "chief ruler of Rosh"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew rosh can mean "chief" or be a place name, as the Septuagint takes it. It bears on how the Gog prophecy is identified.

records.change: "chief prince" becomes "chief ruler of Rosh"
records.note: The same choice as 38:3: rosh read as a place name, following the Septuagint, rather than as "chief".

records.change: "the Son of God" becomes "a son of the gods"
records.note: Translation choice: the Aramaic bar elahin can be read either way, and Nebuchadnezzar was a pagan speaker. The KJV's reading lets the fourth figure be taken as the pre-incarnate Christ; the MKJV's does not.

records.change: Thrones "cast down" become thrones "set in place"
records.note: The Aramaic verb can mean "cast" or "placed"; the MKJV has thrones set up for judgment rather than earthly thrones overthrown.

records.change: "a covenant"; abominations "on a corner of the altar"; poured on "the desolator"
records.note: Translation choices in difficult Hebrew; the MKJV's wording bears on whether the verse is read of Christ or of an antichrist figure, and has judgment fall on the desolator rather than the desolate.

records.change: "the God of forces" becomes "the god of forces"
records.note: The Hebrew eloah can be either; the KJV's capital suggests the true God, the MKJV's lower case a false god of fortresses.

records.change: "God" and "your God" not written; "I will not be for you"
records.note: The Hebrew says "and he said" and "I will not be (ehyeh) for you"; the KJV supplies "God" and "your God" in italics. The MKJV's literal reading can echo the divine name "I AM".

records.change: "like men" becomes "like Adam"
records.note: The Hebrew ke'adam can mean "like men" or "like Adam"; the MKJV's reading implies a covenant made with Adam, which the KJV's does not.

records.change: "Moloch" becomes "your king"; "your god" becomes "your gods"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew malkekem can mean "your king" or name the god Molech, as the Septuagint and Acts 7:43 read it.

records.change: "hell" becomes "Sheol"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew sheol is transliterated rather than rendered "hell"; the words are the same underneath.

records.change: "O mighty God" becomes "my Rock"
records.note: The Hebrew tsur means "rock", a title of God; the KJV renders its sense as "mighty God". God is still addressed either way.

records.change: "hell" becomes "Sheol"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew sheol is transliterated rather than rendered "hell".

records.change: "having salvation" becomes "victorious"
records.note: Translation choice over the Hebrew nosha (saved, delivered). In this messianic verse, quoted in Matthew 21:5, the KJV's wording ties the King to salvation.

records.change: "I am Christ" rendered "I AM"
records.note: The Greek has only "egō eimi" and the KJV supplies "Christ" in italics; the MKJV renders it as the divine name. A translation choice: the deceivers claim God's name rather than the title Messiah.

records.change: "them that believe" becomes "those believing these things"
records.note: The Greek "tauta" (these) goes with "signs" in the KJV ("these signs"); the MKJV attaches it to believing. A translation choice that shifts the object of faith to the preceding words.

records.change: "I am Christ" as "I AM"; "time draweth near" as "has come"
records.note: The Greek has "egō eimi" and "ēngiken"; the KJV supplies "Christ" and reads the nearness as future. The MKJV makes the deceivers claim the divine name and announce the time as arrived; a translation choice.

records.change: "hell" becomes "Hades"
records.note: The Greek is "hadēs" in both texts; the MKJV transliterates where the KJV translates. A translation choice about the place of the dead, not a textual difference.

records.change: "hell" becomes "Hades"
records.note: The Greek is "hadēs" in both texts; the MKJV transliterates where the KJV translates. Christ's resurrection from the place of the dead is stated the same way.

records.change: "Jesus" becomes "Joshua"
records.note: Both translate the same Greek name (Iēsous); the MKJV supplies the historical referent, Joshua son of Nun, who brought the tabernacle into Canaan. No doctrine is affected.

records.change: Question adds "not", inviting the answer yes
records.note: The Greek question begins with "mē", which expects the answer no, as the KJV renders it; the MKJV's "not" reads the other way, though "Let it not be!" still follows.

records.change: Question adds "not", inviting the answer yes
records.note: The Greek question begins with "mē", which expects the answer no, as the KJV renders it; the MKJV's "not" reads the other way, though "Let it not be!" still follows.

records.change: Question adds "not", inviting the answer yes
records.note: The Greek question begins with "mē", which expects the answer no, as the KJV renders it; the MKJV's "not" reads the other way, though "Let it not be!" still follows.

records.change: Omits the subscription naming Corinth and Phebe
records.note: The subscription is a later scribal note printed in KJV editions, not part of the letter in the Greek text; the MKJV prints only the closing words.

records.change: "keep his virgin" becomes "keep his virginity"
records.note: The Greek "parthenos" can mean a virgin daughter or betrothed, or virginity; the MKJV reads it of the man's own celibacy. A translation choice that changes who the verse concerns.

records.change: Omits the subscription naming Philippi and the bearers
records.note: The subscription is a later scribal note printed in KJV editions, not part of the letter in the Greek text; the MKJV prints only the closing words.

records.change: "the Saviour of all men" becomes "the preserver"
records.note: The Greek "sōtēr" is the usual word for Saviour; the MKJV renders it "preserver", reading the verse of God's providential care. A translation choice; God as Saviour is still stated in 1 Timothy 1:1 and 2:3.

records.change: Omits the subscription naming Laodicea
records.note: The subscription is a later scribal note printed in KJV editions, not part of the letter in the Greek text; the MKJV prints only the closing words.

records.change: Omits the subscription naming Timotheus as first bishop and Rome

records.change: Omits the subscription naming Titus as bishop of Crete
records.note: The subscription is a later scribal note printed in KJV editions, not part of the letter in the Greek text; the MKJV prints only the closing words.

records.change: Omits the subscription naming Rome and Onesimus
records.note: The subscription is a later scribal note printed in KJV editions, not part of the letter in the Greek text; the MKJV prints only the closing words.

records.change: "Jesus" becomes "Joshua"
records.note: Both translate the same Greek name (Iēsous); the MKJV supplies the historical referent, Joshua son of Nun, since the passage concerns the entry into Canaan. No doctrine is affected.

records.change: Omits the subscription "Written to the Hebrews from Italy"
records.note: The subscription is a later scribal note printed in KJV editions, not part of the letter in the Greek text; the MKJV prints only the closing words.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "our Lord Christ"
records.note: "Iēsou" is in the Textus Receptus and the critical text alike, so the omission looks like the MKJV's own; Christ is still called "the Lord of glory" in the verse.

records.change: "hell" becomes "Tartarus"
records.note: The Greek verb "tartaroō" names Tartarus; the MKJV transliterates where the KJV translates "hell". A translation choice; the judgment of the fallen angels is stated the same way.

records.change: "that spirit of antichrist" becomes "the antichrist"
records.note: The Greek "to tou antichristou" means "that [spirit] of the antichrist"; the MKJV drops the implied "spirit", making the verse speak of the person rather than his spirit. A translation choice.

records.change: "the only Lord God, and our Lord" read as one person
records.note: Both follow the Textus Receptus ("despotēn theon kai kyrion"); the MKJV applies one article to both titles, so "Master, God" names Jesus Christ, where the KJV can be read as two persons. A translation choice.
